summary: ES dossier delivered per DOSSIER_TEMPLATE (all 7 sections, every claim tagged FACT/OBSERVED/POSTULATED/NOT_RUN). Descriptive statistics computed from legal raw per-contract daily data (10 ES contracts, RTH bars, useRTH=true) with strict past/rolling windows; no PnL, no parameter selection, no scored runs. Primary-source checks: CFTC CoT schedule, BLS CPI+NFP schedules, FOMC 2026 calendar fetched directly (URLs + access date 2026-10-02 in dossier); CME direct remains blocked (HTTP 403/timeout) - specs evidenced via machine identity (S1), NinjaTrader/AMP mirrors and cmegroup.com search snippets, each labeled with channel. Key measured findings: (1) at the data lane's declared roll date (last session before expiry month) the old front still trades ~1M contracts/RTH-day while the next quarterly trades <2k - the declared rule rolls ~2 weeks before the market's liquidity migration; next contract reaches front-scale volume (>=100k/day) 4-5 sessions before old expiry in all 5 cycles 2025-06..2026-09 (roll week), and the declared-rule front is a thin (<100k) book for ~8-9 sessions each quarter; (2) all 5 observed adjacent-contract roll gaps positive (+52.5..+67.75 pts, ~0.76-0.86%/quarter, ~3.3%/yr) - unadjusted chains embed these jumps, back-adjustment mandatory for level/trend work; (3) June expiries deviate from 3rd Friday due to Juneteenth (ESM6 2026-06-18, ESM7 2027-06-17) - naive 3rd-Friday rules are wrong for June; (4) front-scale era 2025-06-13..2026-10-01 (284 days, robustness-checked volume cutoff): median front volume 1.09M/day, daily ret std 0.77% (ann 12.2% descriptor), overnight->RTH-open gap std 0.48% (~63% of daily variance arrives at the open); single-regime (rally) caveat; (5) front BID/ASK close-proxy spread median 1 tick ($12.50), p90 2 ticks, 0 crossed days (284 front days); deferred-quote rot excluded via front-only filter; (6) RTH hourly volume profile (30 days): 09:00 CT 18.4% and 14:00 CT 19.7% dominate; overnight Globex absent from all files (useRTH) - overnight session behavior NOT_RUN; (7) exact old-vs-new volume crossover unobservable (each expired contract's raw file ends at its declared roll date).
findings: Declared roll rule (last session before day-1 of expiry month) exits the ES front ~2 weeks before the market's liquidity migration: at every declared roll 2025-06..2026-09 old front carried 0.98-1.34M/day vs next ~0.5-2k; next quarterly ramps to >=100k/day 4-5 sessions before old expiry (2025-09-15, 2025-12-12, 2026-03-13, 2026-06-11, 2026-09-14). Recommend engine default T-5 calendar roll (deterministic, PIT-safe) or A/B vs declared rule; volume-crossover roll not measurable in this snapshot.

Roll gaps all positive: +55.75/+58.75/+52.5/+61.75/+67.75 pts (~0.76-0.86%/quarter) at the 5 declared rolls; consistent with carry (rates > dividend yield, POSTULATED mechanism). Unadjusted continuous series embed ~+0.8%/quarter artificial jumps - back-adjust or exclude roll-boundary returns (dossier H2, engine-relevant).

June expiry is NOT 3rd Friday when Juneteenth observance interferes (ESM6 2026-06-18, ESM7 2027-06-17, computed from S1 lastTradeDate across 26 contracts; all other months are 3rd Fridays). Roll/expiry code must special-case June.

All raw intraday files are useRTH=true (RTH 08:30-16:00 CT bars only): overnight Globex session is absent from the snapshot; overnight behavior measurable only as RTH-open gap (std 0.48% in front-scale era = ~63% of daily return std). Engine and any session-based research must account for this.

Front-scale era is a single macro regime (persistent rally, ~+27% level, ann-vol descriptor 12.2%); no crisis sample; |ret| lag-1 autocorr 0.002 in this era vs 0.152 on the full settlement-derived chain - regime breadth is the binding constraint for all behavior claims.
